title: الْخُبِيرْ
genre: Moroccan Darija horror, one tale (khbira) per episode
premise: One tale (khbira) per episode on a single case: an abandoned riad in the old medina with a well that sings. A first-person storyteller narrates; he is NOT called the Expert. 'الخبير' means fictional stories in Moroccan Darija. Folk beliefs used: jinn live in wells and drains and imitate voices; never answer your name at night; bismillah before entering or pouring; salt, jawi incense (bakhour), hamsa, chouafa, taleb reading Quran.
style: found-footage horror photograph at night, one weak flashlight beam, authentic old Moroccan medina setting: zellige mosaic tiles, carved plaster and cedar, iron-studded wooden doors, brass lanterns, worn rugs, heavy film grain, crushed blacks, desaturated, photorealistic, absolutely no text, no letters, no numbers, no timestamps, no watermarks, vertical composition
logline: الْخُبِيرْ: حِكَايَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ، بَيْتٌ وَاحِدٌ، عَشْرُ حَلَقَاتٍ.

arc.title: الخبيرة الأولى: البئر
arc.summary: An abandoned riad in the old medina; neighbours hear a little girl singing from an upper floor that no longer exists. The Expert enters alone and finds a covered well.
arc.cliffhanger: His own recording shows him standing at the well, singing in the girl's voice.

arc.title: الخبيرة الثانية: الجار
arc.summary: The neighbour who vanished after he answered the voice from the well; his family speaks.
arc.cliffhanger: A voice on the family's phone says the Expert's name.

arc.title: الخبيرة الثالثة: الاسم
arc.summary: He replays the recording every night; between the verses of the song a whisper says his own name. He remembers his grandmother's rule: if you are called by name at night, never answer, because jinn imitate voices and an answer shows them the way in. He burns jawi incense as she used to.
arc.cliffhanger: The voice at the door calls the name of his brother, Younes.

arc.title: الخبيرة الرابعة: الشوافة
arc.summary: He goes to an old chouafa in the derb. She burns bakhour, the smoke bends toward his shadow, she refuses to say what is in the well and gives one order: bring salt and a taleb.
arc.cliffhanger: She says the well has already taken one voice from his family, and it is asking for the second.

arc.title: الخبيرة الخامسة: الطالب
arc.summary: A taleb agrees to recite Quran at the riad at fajr. The well repeats every verse back, a half-second late and in a child's voice.
arc.cliffhanger: The taleb leaves in silence; that night his own voice comes out of the well.

arc.title: الخبيرة السادسة: الصورة
arc.summary: A 30-year-old photograph in the neighbours' shop shows a man who looks like him standing at the riad door with a camera.
arc.cliffhanger: The man in the photograph is holding a camera, and the light on it is red.

arc.title: الخبيرة السابعة: الأخ
arc.summary: His brother Younes went into the riad in 1994 and never came out; his mother still keeps Younes's slippers by the door.
arc.cliffhanger: His brother's voice answers from the well, calling him by his childhood nickname.

arc.title: الخبيرة الثامنة: الفريق
arc.summary: He returns with cousins and a neighbour, salt on the threshold, the taleb's amulet; they answer the well one by one.
arc.cliffhanger: Only he is left, and the well is quiet.

arc.title: الخبيرة التاسعة: القواعد
arc.summary: His grandmother's sayings turn out to be the rules of the well: never answer your name at night, say bismillah before you pour or enter, salt on the threshold, never look into water at midnight. It wants a voice, not a body.
arc.cliffhanger: It wants a voice, not a body.

arc.title: الخبيرة العاشرة: الأخير
arc.summary: He goes down with the phone recording. The last file is recorded by whoever answers.
arc.cliffhanger: The final recording is not in his voice.
